/home/shobhitg/src/multi-team-support/scripts/debug.lua

For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

Include even tiny strings ("OK", "Cancel", "+", "▶", "×"). For icon/symbol-only strings add hazard 'symbol-only'. Do NOT report: code comments, table keys, event/style/prototype identifier names used only as identifiers, file paths, pattern strings for string.find, storage keys.

Per string, set:
- status: 'localised' if it is already a {"section.key", ...} locale reference, 'partial' if a locale reference is concatenated/mixed with hardcoded English, 'hardcoded' otherwise.
- dynamic: describe exactly how it is assembled if not static — every '..' concatenation, string.format, table.concat, tick-to-time formatting, number formatting, player/team name interpolation. This is critical: concatenated sentences are the main localisation hazard.
- visibility: 'player' (any player sees it), 'admin' (admin-only), 'debug' (behind a debug flag), 'external' (leaves the game: Discord, RCON, files), 'log-only'.
- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

139	--- Re-create a captured equipment layout inside one specific stack. Each put
140	--- is pcall'd so one equipment name removed by a mod change doesn't void the
141	--- rest of the grid.
142	local function fill_grid(stack, grid)
143	    if not stack.grid then return end
144	    for _, eq in pairs(grid) do
145	        pcall(function()
146	            local placed = stack.grid.put{
147	                name     = eq.name,
148	                position = eq.position,
149	                quality  = eq.quality,
150	            }

152	        end)
153	    end

156	--- Create one grid-bearing item (in practice: armor) in a slot we pick, and
157	--- return that exact stack.
158	---
159	--- Placement is by handle rather than a name search after the fact. The player
160	--- can already be carrying a same-named armor -- worn, or granted by a starter
161	--- mod such as FasterStart -- and a post-insert search lands on whichever stack
162	--- it happens to reach first, loading the armor they already had and leaving
163	--- the one we just granted empty.
164	---
165	--- The armor slot is tried first so the kit arrives worn; anything that will
166	--- not go there (already occupied, or a grid item that is not armor) falls back
167	--- to the first free main-inventory slot. Returns nil when there is no room.
168	local function place_grid_item(player, name, quality)
169	    local spec = {name = name, count = 1, quality = quality}
170	    local armor_inv = player.get_inventory(defines.inventory.character_armor)
171	    -- can_insert respects the slot filter, so a grid item that is not armor
172	    -- (a spidertron, say) is rejected here rather than by set_stack.
173	    if armor_inv and armor_inv.is_empty() and armor_inv.can_insert(spec)
174	       and armor_inv[1].set_stack(spec) then
175	        return armor_inv[1]
176	    end
177	    local main = player.get_inventory(defines.inventory.character_main)
178	    local slot = main and main.find_empty_stack()
179	    if slot and slot.set_stack(spec) then return slot end
180	    return nil
181	end

184	--- when the entry carries a captured grid. The engine insert gets a clean
185	--- {name, count, quality} table -- entry tables can carry extra fields (grid)
186	--- that ItemStackIdentification would reject.
187	function M.insert_starter_item(player, item)
188	    pcall(function()
189	        local count = item.count or 1
190	        if item.grid then
191	            -- Only one layout was captured, so only the first copy is loaded;
192	            -- any further copies are inserted plain, as before.
193	            local stack = place_grid_item(player, item.name, item.quality)
194	            if stack then
195	                fill_grid(stack, item.grid)
196	                if count > 1 then
197	                    player.insert{name = item.name, count = count - 1, quality = item.quality}
198	                end
199	                return
200	            end
201	        end
202	        player.insert{name = item.name, count = count, quality = item.quality}
203	    end)

251	    if not grid then return nil end
252	    local out = {}
253	    for _, eq in pairs(grid.equipment) do
254	        out[#out + 1] = {
255	            name     = eq.name,
256	            position = {x = eq.position.x, y = eq.position.y},
257	            quality  = eq.quality and eq.quality.name or nil,
258	            energy   = eq.energy > 0 and eq.energy or nil,
259	        }
260	    end
261	    if #out == 0 then return nil end
262	    return out
263	end
264	
265	--- Record the equipment layout of `stack` on `entry`, along with the stack's own
266	--- quality. Grid layouts are quality-specific -- a higher-quality armor has a
267	--- bigger grid -- so a copy granted at normal quality would silently drop every
268	--- equipment whose captured position falls outside it. Quality is carried only
269	--- for grid-bearing entries; plain items keep the existing name-only merge.
270	local function adopt_grid(entry, stack)
271	    entry.grid = serialize_grid(stack)
272	    if entry.grid then
273	        entry.quality = stack.quality and stack.quality.name or nil
274	    end
275	end
276	
277	--- Collect all items from a player's character inventories. Entries are
278	--- {name, count} plus an optional `grid` (equipment layout) and the `quality`
279	--- it was captured at, taken from the first stack of that name that carries one.
280	function M.collect_character_items(player)
281	    local items, seen = {}, {}
282	    if not player.character then return items end
283	    for _, inv_type in pairs({
284	        defines.inventory.character_main,
285	        defines.inventory.character_guns,
286	        defines.inventory.character_ammo,
287	        defines.inventory.character_armor,
288	    }) do
289	        local inv = player.get_inventory(inv_type)
290	        if inv then
291	            for i = 1, #inv do
292	                local stack = inv[i]
293	                if stack and stack.valid_for_read then
294	                    local entry = seen[stack.name]
295	                    if entry then
296	                        entry.count = entry.count + stack.count
297	                        if not entry.grid then adopt_grid(entry, stack) end
298	                    else
299	                        entry = {name = stack.name, count = stack.count}
300	                        adopt_grid(entry, stack)
301	                        seen[stack.name] = entry
302	                        items[#items + 1] = entry
303	                    end
304	                end
305	            end
306	        end
307	    end
308	    table.sort(items, function(a, b) return a.name < b.name end)
309	    return items
310	end
311	
312	--- Auto-populate starter items from the first spawning player's inventory. This
313	--- captures the map's default loadout into the admin list. Under a delivery
314	--- override (e.g. Brave New MTS) the same capture is what pre-populates the list
315	--- that then gets routed to team logistic chests instead of player inventories
316	--- (the spawning character is emptied separately, in on_player_created).
317	function M.auto_populate_starter_items(player)
318	    if storage.starter_items then return end
319	    if not player.character then return end
320	    storage.starter_items = M.collect_character_items(player)
321	    if #storage.starter_items > 0 then
322	        log("[multi-team-support] auto-populated starter items from " .. player.name
323	            .. " (" .. #storage.starter_items .. " item types)")
324	    end
325	end
326	
327	return M
328

2	-- Disable external blueprint imports (string paste, library, import-string
3	-- button) on the Default permission group while leaving in-game blueprint
4	-- creation (alt-shift-click, copy-paste of placed entities) untouched.

7	-- below fire ONLY when an external import is being confirmed:

9	--     (toolbar button and the dialog that opens on chat paste).

11	--     the library) into the cursor / inventory.

13	--     filtered variant used when a filter is set on the import.
14	--   - open_blueprint_library_gui: opens the personal/server blueprint
15	--     library.

17	-- unaffected.
18	--

23	local M = {}
24	
25	local BLOCKED_ACTIONS = {
26	    defines.input_action.import_blueprint_string,

39	end
40

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/buddy_store.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Low-level store for pending buddy requests. Deliberately dependency-free (no
6	-- require of force_utils/team_slots/pen_gui) so both the buddy-request GUI and
7	-- team_slots can call it without a circular require — force_utils requires
8	-- team_slots, so anything team_slots pulls in must not lead back to force_utils.
9	--
10	-- A request is keyed by the REQUESTER's player index and its value is the
11	-- TEAM's force name (not a leader player index) — that is what lets ANY online
12	-- member of the team accept it. The Accept/Reject dialog is a per-requester
13	-- screen frame (sb_buddy_req_<requester_index>) shown to every online member,
14	-- so several pending requests coexist and are torn down individually.
15	--
16	-- Storage:
17	--   storage.buddy_requests[requester_index] = force_name  -- pending request
18	
19	local buddy_store = {}
20	
21	local FRAME_PREFIX = "sb_buddy_req_"
22	
23	--- Screen-frame name for one requester's Accept/Reject dialog.
24	function buddy_store.frame_name(requester_index)
25	    return FRAME_PREFIX .. requester_index
26	end
27	
28	--- The team a pen player is currently requesting to join, or nil.
29	function buddy_store.request_of(requester_index)
30	    return (storage.buddy_requests or {})[requester_index]
31	end
32	
33	--- Record a pending request (requester -> team force name).
34	function buddy_store.set(requester_index, force_name)
35	    storage.buddy_requests = storage.buddy_requests or {}
36	    storage.buddy_requests[requester_index] = force_name
37	end
38	
39	--- Destroy one requester's Accept/Reject frame on every connected player's
40	--- screen (members hold these frames; the requester never does).
41	function buddy_store.destroy_frames(requester_index)
42	    local fname = buddy_store.frame_name(requester_index)
43	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
44	        local f = p.gui.screen[fname]
45	        if f then f.destroy() end
46	    end
47	end
48	
49	--- Drop one request and tear down its frames.
50	function buddy_store.clear(requester_index)
51	    if storage.buddy_requests then storage.buddy_requests[requester_index] = nil end
52	    buddy_store.destroy_frames(requester_index)
53	end
54	
55	--- Cancel every request addressed to a team (its slot is being released, so the
56	--- requests can no longer be accepted there). Returns the affected requester
57	--- indices so the caller can notify them / refresh their pen GUI.
58	function buddy_store.clear_for_team(force_name)
59	    local affected = {}
60	    if not storage.buddy_requests then return affected end
61	    for req_idx, fn in pairs(storage.buddy_requests) do
62	        if fn == force_name then
63	            affected[#affected + 1] = req_idx
64	            storage.buddy_requests[req_idx] = nil
65	            buddy_store.destroy_frames(req_idx)
66	        end
67	    end
68	    return affected
69	end
70	
71	--- Destroy every buddy-request frame on one player's screen, whichever
72	--- requester they belong to (used when a member returns to the pen / is
73	--- removed, so they stop holding accept dialogs for their old team).
74	function buddy_store.destroy_all_frames_for(player)
75	    if not (player and player.valid) then return end
76	    for _, child in pairs(player.gui.screen.children) do
77	        if child.name and child.name:find("^" .. FRAME_PREFIX) then child.destroy() end
78	    end
79	end
80	
81	--- The team a player really belongs to, seeing through a temporary spectator
82	--- force (a member remote-viewing another surface is on the "spectator" force
83	--- but still a member of their team). Mirrors spectator.get_effective_force as a
84	--- pure storage read so this module stays dependency-free.
85	function buddy_store.team_of(player)
86	    return (storage.spectator_real_force or {})[player.index] or player.force.name
87	end
88	
89	--- Count online members of a team, INCLUDING any who are currently spectating
90	--- (force.connected_players would miss them). Used to decide whether a team is
91	--- joinable and to deliver Accept dialogs.
92	function buddy_store.online_member_count(force_name)
93	    local n = 0
94	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
95	        if buddy_store.team_of(p) == force_name then n = n + 1 end
96	    end
97	    return n
98	end
99	
100	--- Drop every pending request and tear down all buddy frames. Called from
101	--- on_configuration_changed so a save upgraded mid-request can't strand a
102	--- requester on a stale entry (the old model stored a leader player index as the
103	--- value; the new model stores a force name). Pending requests are ephemeral, so
104	--- clearing them on a mod update is safe.
105	function buddy_store.reset()
106	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
107	        buddy_store.destroy_all_frames_for(p)
108	    end
109	    storage.buddy_requests = {}
110	end
111	
112	return buddy_store
113

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/chat_channel.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Chat privacy channel: "global" (default) or "local" (team-only).
6	--
7	-- SCOPE. The admin flag individual_chat_enabled decides who one switch moves:
8	--   team scope (default) — the whole TEAM moves together. Syncing per team
9	--     removes the asymmetric-conversation leak where one member asks in
10	--     team-only mode and a teammate still in global mode answers for the
11	--     whole server to read.
12	--   individual scope — each PLAYER carries their own channel. That leak comes
13	--     back by construction, which is why it stayed off until the chat badge
14	--     (scripts/chat_tag.lua) put each message's channel in the line itself: a
15	--     teammate can now see they are about to answer in the open.
16	--
17	-- Each scope keeps its own storage. A team's setting survives a round trip;
18	-- the per-player table is re-seeded from it on every flip to individual, so
19	-- an individual choice does not outlive an admin flipping scope back and
20	-- forth. Flips migrate in the privacy-preserving direction only — see
21	-- M.on_scope_change.
22	--
23	-- The engine's native chat delivery (sender's force only) IS team chat; the
24	-- channel only decides whether events/chat.lua relays a message beyond it.
25	-- Pen spectators are always global — no state, no toggle. A team-only member
26	-- can shout one message globally by starting it with "!".
27	--
28	-- Requires helpers and admin_flags, both of which are themselves leaves, so
29	-- spectator core, the HUD, and the chat event handler can all require this
30	-- without closing a cycle.
31	--
32	-- Storage shape (absent = global, the default, in both):
33	--   storage.chat_channel[force_name]          = "local"   -- team scope
34	--   storage.chat_channel_player[player_index] = "local"   -- individual scope
35	
36	local helpers     = require("scripts.helpers")
37	local admin_flags = require("scripts.admin_flags")
38	
39	local M = {}
40	
41	-- Fixed per-mode colors, for muscle memory: green encourages the global
42	-- default; team-only is a calm blue (deliberately not red). Every rendering
43	-- of channel state -- the switch announcements below, the chat badge in
44	-- scripts/chat_tag.lua, the spectate disclosure -- reads these, so retuning
45	-- one constant retunes all of them.
46	M.GLOBAL_COLOR = {0.4, 0.9, 0.4}
47	M.LOCAL_COLOR  = {0.45, 0.8, 1}
48	
49	-- Soft blip when a spectating member's team message was also visible to
50	-- co-spectators. (Channel switches deliberately play no sound — the printed
51	-- announcement is enough.)
52	M.SOUND_EXPOSURE = "utility/list_box_click"
53	
54	--- Effective-force resolution without requiring spectator (leaf constraint):
55	--- same inline pattern as remote_api's effective_fn.
56	local function effective_fn(p)
57	    return (storage.spectator_real_force or {})[p.index]
58	        or (p.force and p.force.name)
59	end
60	
61	--- Is the feature currently individual-scoped? Team scope is the default, so
62	--- an unset flag and a save from before the switch existed both read as team.
63	function M.is_individual()
64	    return admin_flags.flag("individual_chat_enabled") == true
65	end
66	
67	--- The storage table and key holding one player's channel under the current
68	--- scope. Both nil when they have no team at all (pen spectators), which is
69	--- what makes "no team means no channel" a single rule here rather than a
70	--- check repeated at every call site.
71	local function slot(player)
72	    local force_name = effective_fn(player)
73	    if not helpers.is_team_force(force_name) then return nil end
74	    if M.is_individual() then
75	        storage.chat_channel_player = storage.chat_channel_player or {}
76	        return storage.chat_channel_player, player.index
77	    end
78	    storage.chat_channel = storage.chat_channel or {}
79	    return storage.chat_channel, force_name
80	end
81	
82	--- Is this player's chat currently team-only? False for anyone without a team.
83	function M.is_local_for(player)
84	    local tbl, key = slot(player)
85	    return tbl ~= nil and tbl[key] == "local"
86	end
87	
88	--- Connected players whose effective force is this team — includes members
89	--- currently force-swapped into spectator mode, who must hear channel
90	--- switches too.
91	local function connected_members(force_name)
92	    local out = {}
93	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
94	        if effective_fn(p) == force_name then out[#out + 1] = p end
95	    end
96	    return out
97	end
98	
99	--- Everyone whose channel moves together with this player's: the whole team
100	--- under team scope, only themselves under individual scope. Callers use it
101	--- both to announce and to refresh HUDs, so the two can never disagree.
102	function M.peers(player)
103	    if M.is_individual() then return {player} end
104	    return connected_members(effective_fn(player))
105	end
106	
107	local function announce(to_local, switcher, individual)
108	    local color = to_local and M.LOCAL_COLOR or M.GLOBAL_COLOR
109	    local state = helpers.colored_name(
110	        to_local and "TEAM-ONLY" or "GLOBAL", color)
111	    local subject
112	    if individual then
113	        subject = "Your chat is now " .. state .. "."
114	    else
115	        subject = "Team chat is now " .. state .. " (switched by "
116	            .. (switcher
117	                and helpers.colored_name(switcher.name, switcher.chat_color)
118	                or "an admin") .. ")."
119	    end
120	    if to_local then
121	        return subject .. " Messages stay within your team; start a message"
122	            .. " with ! to shout globally."
123	    end
124	    return subject .. " Everyone on the server sees your messages."
125	end
126	
127	--- Set this player's channel outright ("local" | "global"). No-op (returns
128	--- false) when it is already there — the switch UI selects rather than
129	--- cycles. On change, announces to everyone the change actually moved;
130	--- callers refresh HUDs for M.peers on true.
131	function M.set_for(player, channel, switcher)
132	    local tbl, key = slot(player)
133	    if not tbl then return false end
134	    local to_local = channel == "local"
135	    if (tbl[key] == "local") == to_local then return false end
136	    tbl[key] = to_local and "local" or nil
137	
138	    local individual = M.is_individual()
139	    local line = announce(to_local, switcher, individual)
140	    for _, member in ipairs(M.peers(player)) do
141	        member.print(line)
142	    end
143	    return true
144	end
145	
146	--- Carry channel state across a scope flip, in the privacy-preserving
147	--- direction only: throwing the admin switch must never silently start
148	--- broadcasting what was private a second earlier.
149	---   → individual: everyone inherits their own team's current channel.
150	---   → team: a team goes team-only if ANY member was individually team-only.
151	---     Most-private wins, because the alternative exposes whoever chose it.
152	--- Both directions count offline players. Being offline does not revoke your
153	--- membership, and excluding them would silently drop a team-only member's
154	--- choice while they were away — exactly the exposure this function exists
155	--- to prevent.
156	function M.on_scope_change(now_individual)
157	    storage.chat_channel        = storage.chat_channel or {}
158	    storage.chat_channel_player = storage.chat_channel_player or {}
159	    for _, p in pairs(game.players) do
160	        local force_name = effective_fn(p)
161	        if helpers.is_team_force(force_name) then
162	            if now_individual then
163	                storage.chat_channel_player[p.index] =
164	                    storage.chat_channel[force_name]
165	            elseif storage.chat_channel_player[p.index] == "local" then
166	                storage.chat_channel[force_name] = "local"
167	            end
168	        end
169	    end
170	end
171	
172	--- Drop a released slot's team channel so a future team starts on the
173	--- default. Only the team-scoped value: an individual channel is a personal
174	--- preference that follows the player to whatever team they join next, and
175	--- resetting it here would silently flip someone who had chosen team-only
176	--- back to broadcasting. Removed players are purged by events/player_removed.
177	function M.on_release(force_name)
178	    if storage.chat_channel then storage.chat_channel[force_name] = nil end
179	end
180	
181	return M
182

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/chat_tag.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Per-message channel badge, stamped onto player.tag.
6	--
7	-- The engine prints every chat message to the sender's own force before any
8	-- mod runs, and that native line cannot be cancelled or edited (see
9	-- events/chat.lua). player.tag is the only handle on it: the engine appends
10	-- the tag after the player's name, so the badge rides along on the one line
11	-- MTS otherwise cannot touch. That makes chat scrollback a record of the
12	-- channel each message was sent under — something the HUD switch, which only
13	-- ever shows the CURRENT state, cannot provide.
14	--
15	-- Both states carry a badge. Marking only one would make absence meaningful,
16	-- and absence is ambiguous: a fresh join, a pen spectator and an admin-moved
17	-- player all look identical to a team gone dark.
18	--
19	-- The tag is also drawn on the map and above multiplayer selection
20	-- rectangles, i.e. opposing teams can read it. That is accepted: a team-only
21	-- badge does tell opponents this team went dark, but the alternative leaks the
22	-- same fact through the badge's absence.
23	--
24	-- One case the badge cannot narrow: a "!" shout goes server-wide without
25	-- changing the channel, so that line still reads [TEAM]. The leading "!" the
26	-- sender typed is right there on the same line and is the marker for it —
27	-- nothing per-message can be stamped after the engine has already printed.
28	
29	local chat_channel = require("scripts.chat_channel")
30	local helpers      = require("scripts.helpers")
31	
32	local M = {}
33	
34	-- count-font is the only vanilla font that both fits the width budget and
35	-- sets border = true (size 13, from default-bold). The black outline is what
36	-- keeps the badge readable over arbitrary terrain in the map view, where an
37	-- unbordered tag washes out; the dark chat panel would not need it.
38	local FONT = "count-font"
39	
40	--- Colors come from chat_channel rather than literals so the badge and the
41	--- printed "Team chat is now ..." announcement can never drift apart.
42	local function badge(color, word)
43	    return ("[color=%s,%s,%s][font=%s][%s][/font][/color]")
44	        :format(color[1], color[2], color[3], FONT, word)
45	end
46	
47	-- Both badges are constant, so build them once at parse time rather than
48	-- reformatting per player per second in the refresh below.
49	local GLOBAL_BADGE = badge(chat_channel.GLOBAL_COLOR, "GLOBAL")
50	local LOCAL_BADGE  = badge(chat_channel.LOCAL_COLOR,  "TEAM")
51	
52	--- The badge for one player's current channel — their team's under team
53	--- scope, their own under individual scope; chat_channel resolves which.
54	--- Players with no team (pen spectators) have no channel to report and get
55	--- "", matching the chat switch, which gui/chat_switch.lua removes for them.
56	function M.badge_for(player, force_name)
57	    if not helpers.is_team_force(force_name) then return "" end
58	    return chat_channel.is_local_for(player) and LOCAL_BADGE or GLOBAL_BADGE
59	end
60	
61	--- Stamp one player's badge from their effective team. force_name is the
62	--- player's effective force, or nil for none.
63	---
64	--- Only writes on change: this runs for every connected player every second,
65	--- and reassigning the tag redraws their nameplate. Always assigns "" rather
66	--- than nil — tag is a string field, and nil would error.
67	function M.update_player(player, force_name)
68	    local want = M.badge_for(player, force_name)
69	    if player.tag ~= want then player.tag = want end
70	end
71	
72	return M
73

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/chunk_trim.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Admin tool: trim unused chunks on team surfaces (every planet a team owns,
6	-- not just nauvis). For each surface, preserves a buffer of chunks around team
7	-- entities, connected players, and spawner corpses; deletes everything else and
8	-- uncharts the deleted chunks. Space platforms are skipped -- their foundation
9	-- is tiles, not entities, so chunk deletion could destroy parts of the platform.
10	--
11	-- For multi-surface runs, surfaces are processed one per tick interval so
12	-- the server can catch up between large trims.
13	--
14	-- Storage shape:
15	--   storage.chunk_trim_queue = {
16	--       surfaces      = {surface_index, ...},
17	--       idx           = integer,
18	--       entity_buffer = integer,
19	--       player_buffer = integer,
20	--       caller_idx    = integer | nil,
21	--   }
22	
23	local helpers       = require("scripts.helpers")
24	local surface_utils = require("scripts.surface_utils")
25	
26	local chunk_trim = {}
27	
28	-- ─── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29	
30	local DEFAULT_ENTITY_BUFFER = 12
31	local DEFAULT_PLAYER_BUFFER = 8
32	local CHUNK_SIZE            = 32
33	
34	-- ─── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	
36	--- The team force that owns a surface, on any planet, or nil. Space platforms
37	--- are treated as un-trimmable (their foundation is tiles, not entities).
38	local function trimmable_owner(surface)
39	    if not (surface and surface.valid) or surface.platform then return nil end
40	    return surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
41	end
42	
43	--- Send a message to the caller if connected, else broadcast.
44	local function notify(caller_idx, msg)
45	    local p = caller_idx and game.get_player(caller_idx)
46	    if p and p.connected then p.print(msg) else game.print(msg) end
47	end
48	
49	--- Trim one surface synchronously. Returns deleted, total.
50	local function trim_surface(surface, entity_buffer, player_buffer, caller_idx)
51	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return 0, 0 end
52	
53	    local team_force = trimmable_owner(surface)
54	    local label      = team_force and helpers.team_tag(team_force) or surface.name
55	    local force      = team_force and game.forces[team_force]
56	    if not (force and force.valid) then
57	        notify(caller_idx, label .. " (" .. surface.name .. "): no team force; skipped")
58	        return 0, 0
59	    end
60	
61	    local keep = {}
62	    local function mark(cx, cy)
63	        keep[cx] = keep[cx] or {}
64	        keep[cx][cy] = true
65	    end
66	    local function mark_buffer(cx, cy, r)
67	        for dx = -r, r do
68	            for dy = -r, r do mark(cx + dx, cy + dy) end
69	        end
70	    end
71	
72	    -- Dilate by entity_buffer PER DISTINCT OCCUPIED CHUNK, not per entity. Many
73	    -- entities share a chunk, so collecting the distinct occupied chunks first
74	    -- (O(entities)) then dilating each once (O(occupied_chunks * (2r+1)^2)) gives
75	    -- the identical keep-set as dilating every entity would, without the
76	    -- O(entities * (2r+1)^2) blowup on a dense base (PF-6).
77	    local occupied = {}
78	    for _, e in pairs(surface.find_entities_filtered{force = force}) do
79	        local cx = math.floor(e.position.x / CHUNK_SIZE)
80	        local cy = math.floor(e.position.y / CHUNK_SIZE)
81	        occupied[cx] = occupied[cx] or {}
82	        occupied[cx][cy] = true
83	    end
84	    for cx, col in pairs(occupied) do
85	        for cy in pairs(col) do mark_buffer(cx, cy, entity_buffer) end
86	    end
87	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
88	        if p.physical_surface == surface then
89	            local pp = p.physical_position
90	            mark_buffer(
91	                math.floor(pp.x / CHUNK_SIZE),
92	                math.floor(pp.y / CHUNK_SIZE),
93	                player_buffer)

95	    end
96	    -- Preserve spawner death markers so biter expansion history isn't lost.
97	    for _, c in pairs(surface.find_entities_filtered{type = "corpse"}) do

99	            mark(math.floor(c.position.x / CHUNK_SIZE),
100	                 math.floor(c.position.y / CHUNK_SIZE))
101	        end

104	    -- Collect the doomed chunk coords in a first pass, THEN delete in a second
105	    -- pass, rather than deleting mid-get_chunks(). delete_chunk's own events are
106	    -- deferred so mutating during iteration is probably safe, but get_chunks()
107	    -- makes no concurrent-mutation guarantee -- separating the passes removes the
108	    -- doubt for free (deletion still lands end-of-tick either way) (ST-4).
109	    local total = 0

111	    for c in surface.get_chunks() do

1	-- scripts/color_fix.lua
2	-- Keep player colours READABLE, NON-BROWN and DISTINCT from each other.
3	--
4	--   * dark colours (low luminance) are brightened toward white -- hard to read
5	--     against the dark chat / GUI background otherwise;
6	--   * brown / muddy-orange colours are pushed to a vivid orange -- they blend
7	--     into Factorio's terrain otherwise;
8	--   * a colour that clashes with another player's is moved to the colour furthest
9	--     from everyone else's, picked from a palette spread across the readable gamut
10	--     (rotating a single player's own hue just makes clashing players pile up in
11	--     the same gap, so we sample the WHOLE gamut instead).
12	--
13	-- Factorio raises NO event when a player changes colour (assigning
14	-- LuaPlayer::color is documented not to fire on_entity_color_changed), so live
15	-- changes are caught by a cheap poll (events/ticks.lua) that only re-fixes a
16	-- player whose colour actually changed -- no flicker once everyone is settled.
17	-- Joins are handled on on_player_joined_game (events/player_lifecycle.lua).
18	
19	local helpers     = require("scripts.helpers")
20	local admin_flags = require("scripts.admin_flags")
21	
22	local M = {}
23	
24	-- ── Tunables ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
25	local DARK     = 0.50    -- perceived luminance below this is "too dark"
26	local TARGET   = 0.65    -- brighten a dark colour up to this luminance
27	local BHMIN    = 20      -- brown = orange hue band (degrees) ...
28	local BHMAX    = 50
29	local BSMIN    = 0.15    -- ... with at least this saturation ...
30	local BVMAX    = 0.80    -- ... and value below this (a vivid orange has V~1)
31	local BSAT     = 0.60    -- browns are rebuilt at this minimum saturation ...
32	local BTV      = 1.00    -- ... and full value -> a bright distinct orange
33	local MINDIST2 = 0.0625  -- colours closer than sqrt(0.0625)=0.25 (RGB) clash
34	local LREAD    = 0.55    -- palette colours must be at least this readable
35	
36	-- ── Colour maths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
37	local function lum(c) return 0.2126 * c.r + 0.7152 * c.g + 0.0722 * c.b end
38	
39	local function normalize(c)
40	    local a = c.a or 1
41	    if math.max(c.r, c.g, c.b, a) > 1 then
42	        return { r = c.r / 255, g = c.g / 255, b = c.b / 255, a = a / 255 }
43	    end
44	    return { r = c.r, g = c.g, b = c.b, a = a }
45	end
46	
47	local function rgb2hsv(c)
48	    local mx = math.max(c.r, c.g, c.b)
49	    local mn = math.min(c.r, c.g, c.b)
50	    local d = mx - mn
51	    local h = 0
52	    if d > 0 then
53	        if mx == c.r then h = ((c.g - c.b) / d) % 6
54	        elseif mx == c.g then h = (c.b - c.r) / d + 2
55	        else h = (c.r - c.g) / d + 4 end
56	        h = h * 60
57	        if h < 0 then h = h + 360 end
58	    end
59	    local s = 0
60	    if mx > 0 then s = d / mx end
61	    return h, s, mx
62	end
63	
64	local function hsv2rgb(h, s, v, a)
65	    local c = v * s
66	    local x = c * (1 - math.abs((h / 60) % 2 - 1))
67	    local m = v - c
68	    local r, g, b
69	    if h < 60 then r, g, b = c, x, 0
70	    elseif h < 120 then r, g, b = x, c, 0
71	    elseif h < 180 then r, g, b = 0, c, x
72	    elseif h < 240 then r, g, b = 0, x, c
73	    elseif h < 300 then r, g, b = x, 0, c
74	    else r, g, b = c, 0, x end
75	    return { r = r + m, g = g + m, b = b + m, a = a }
76	end
77	
78	local function brighten(c, t)
79	    local L = lum(c)
80	    if L >= t then return c end
81	    local k = (t - L) / (1 - L)
82	    return { r = c.r + k * (1 - c.r), g = c.g + k * (1 - c.g), b = c.b + k * (1 - c.b), a = c.a }
83	end
84	
85	local function dist2(a, b)
86	    local dr = a.r - b.r local dg = a.g - b.g local db = a.b - b.b
87	    return dr * dr + dg * dg + db * db
88	end
89	
90	local function differs(a, b)
91	    return math.abs(a.r - b.r) + math.abs(a.g - b.g) + math.abs(a.b - b.b) > 0.001
92	end
93	
94	-- Palette of distinct, readable colours spread across the gamut. Built once.
95	local palette = {}
96	for hue = 0, 359, 12 do
97	    local svs = { { 0.55, 0.90 }, { 0.80, 1.00 }, { 0.95, 0.80 }, { 0.35, 1.00 } }
98	    for _, sv in ipairs(svs) do
99	        local cand = hsv2rgb(hue, sv[1], sv[2], 0.5)
100	        if lum(cand) >= LREAD then palette[#palette + 1] = cand end
101	    end
102	end
103	
104	local function mindist(c, taken)
105	    local md = 1e9
106	    for _, t in pairs(taken) do
107	        local d = dist2(c, t)
108	        if d < md then md = d end
109	    end
110	    return md
111	end
112	
113	-- The palette colour furthest from everything in `taken`.
114	local function farthest(taken, alpha)
115	    local best, score = palette[1], -1
116	    for _, cand in ipairs(palette) do
117	        local md = mindist(cand, taken)
118	        if md > score then score = md best = cand end
119	    end
120	    return { r = best.r, g = best.g, b = best.b, a = alpha }
121	end
122	
123	-- Brighten darks, push browns to vivid orange. Returns (colour, reason).
124	local function readable(c)
125	    local h, s, v = rgb2hsv(c)
126	    if h >= BHMIN and h <= BHMAX and s >= BSMIN and v <= BVMAX then
127	        -- Rebuild as a vivid orange. A RED-leaning brown can still come out below
128	        -- the readability floor (red has low luminance), so lift it to TARGET --
129	        -- this also keeps the result stable (it won't re-trigger the dark rule).
130	        local nc = hsv2rgb(h, math.max(s, BSAT), BTV, c.a)
131	        if lum(nc) < TARGET then nc = brighten(nc, TARGET) end
132	        return nc, "brown"
133	    elseif lum(c) < DARK then
134	        return brighten(c, TARGET), "dark"
135	    end
136	    return c, "keep"
137	end
138	
139	-- Colours of every player EXCEPT `skip_index` (the live set to differ from).
140	local function other_colours(skip_index)
141	    local out = {}
142	    for _, q in pairs(game.players) do
143	        if q.index ~= skip_index then out[#out + 1] = normalize(q.color) end
144	    end
145	    return out
146	end
147	
148	-- ── Public ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
149	
150	--- Make ONE player's colour readable, non-brown and distinct from everyone
151	--- else. Sets both color (map tint) and chat_color (name). Returns (colour,
152	--- reason) if it changed, else nil. Idempotent -- a good colour is left alone.
153	function M.fix_player(player)
154	    if not (player and player.valid) then return nil end
155	    storage.color_fix_last = storage.color_fix_last or {}
156	    local c = normalize(player.color)
157	    local nc, why = readable(c)
158	    local taken = other_colours(player.index)
159	    if mindist(nc, taken) < MINDIST2 then
160	        nc = farthest(taken, c.a)
161	        why = (why == "keep") and "clash" or (why .. "+clash")
162	    end
163	    if differs(nc, c) then
164	        player.color = nc
165	        player.chat_color = nc
166	        storage.color_fix_last[player.index] = nc
167	        return nc, why
168	    end
169	    storage.color_fix_last[player.index] = c
170	    return nil
171	end
172	
173	local function notify(player, nc)
174	    player.print("Your colour was adjusted to stay readable and distinct from other players.", { color = nc })
175	end
176	
177	--- On-join: brighten/de-brown/de-clash immediately so a dark or duplicate name
178	--- never shows. Gated by the "Readable Player Colours" admin flag.
179	function M.on_joined(player)
180	    if not admin_flags.flag("color_fix_enabled") then return end
181	    local nc = M.fix_player(player)
182	    if nc then notify(player, nc) end
183	end
184	
185	--- Poll for colour changes (no engine event exists). Only re-fixes a connected
186	--- player whose colour differs from what we last set -- a no-op when settled.
187	function M.poll()
188	    if not admin_flags.flag("color_fix_enabled") then return end
189	    storage.color_fix_last = storage.color_fix_last or {}
190	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
191	        local last = storage.color_fix_last[p.index]
192	        if (not last) or differs(normalize(p.color), last) then
193	            local nc = M.fix_player(p)
194	            if nc then notify(p, nc) end
195	        end
196	    end
197	end
198	
199	--- Admin "/mts-fixcolors": re-spread EVERY player from scratch in one clean pass
200	--- (first of any clash keeps its colour, the rest fan out). Announces a summary.
201	function M.fix_all(caller)
202	    storage.color_fix_last = storage.color_fix_last or {}
203	    local taken, names = {}, {}
204	    for _, p in pairs(game.players) do
205	        local c = normalize(p.color)
206	        local nc = readable(c)
207	        if mindist(nc, taken) < MINDIST2 then nc = farthest(taken, c.a) end
208	        taken[#taken + 1] = nc
209	        storage.color_fix_last[p.index] = nc
210	        if differs(nc, c) then
211	            p.color = nc
212	            p.chat_color = nc
213	            names[#names + 1] = p.name
214	        end
215	    end
216	    if #names > 0 then
217	        helpers.broadcast("[colour] Adjusted unreadable / clashing colours for: " .. table.concat(names, ", "))
218	    end
219	    if caller then caller.print(("Adjusted %d player(s)."):format(#names)) end
220	    return #names
221	end
222	
223	return M

11	    "    --players defaults to caller. --delay N inserts N ticks between each (default 0).",

17	local function split_flags(tokens, start_idx, flag_names)
18	    local positional, flags = {}, {}
19	    local i = start_idx
20	    while i <= #tokens do
21	        local t = tokens[i]
22	        local name = t:match("^%-%-(.+)$")
23	        if name and flag_names[name] then
24	            flags[name] = tokens[i + 1]
25	            i = i + 2
26	        else
27	            positional[#positional + 1] = t
28	            i = i + 1
29	        end
30	    end
31	    return positional, flags

34	local function resolve_players(list_str, caller)
35	    if not list_str or list_str == "" then
36	        return caller and {caller} or nil
37	    end
38	    local players = {}
39	    for name in list_str:gmatch("[^,%s]+") do
40	        local p = game.get_player(name)
41	        if not p then
42	            caller.print("Player '" .. name .. "' not found.")

53	        function(cmd)

55	            if not caller then game.print("This command can only be used by a player."); return end
56	            if not caller.admin then caller.print("Only admins can use /mts-debug."); return end
57	
58	            local tokens = {}
59	            for tok in (cmd.parameter or ""):gmatch("%S+") do tokens[#tokens + 1] = tok end
60	
61	            local sub = tokens[1]
62	            if not sub or sub == "help" then caller.print(DEBUG_HELP); return end
63	
64	            if sub == "list" then
65	                local rows = debug_engine.list()
66	                if #rows == 0 then caller.print("[mts-debug] No tasks queued."); return end
67	                local lines = {"[mts-debug] Tasks:"}
68	                for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
69	                    lines[#lines + 1] = string.format("  #%d  %s  %s  (%s)",
70	                        r.id, r.kind, r.label, r.detail)
71	                end
72	                caller.print(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
73	                return
74	            end
75	
76	            if sub == "stop" then
77	                local arg = tokens[2]
78	                if not arg then caller.print("Usage: /mts-debug stop <id|all>"); return end
79	                if arg == "all" then
80	                    local n = debug_engine.stop_all()
81	                    caller.print("[mts-debug] Stopped " .. n .. " task(s).")
82	                else

84	                    if not id then caller.print("Invalid task id: " .. arg); return end

86	                        caller.print("[mts-debug] Stopped task #" .. id .. ".")
87	                    else
88	                        caller.print("[mts-debug] No such task: #" .. id .. ".")
89	                    end
90	                end
91	                return
92	            end
93	
94	            if sub == "research" then
95	                local positional, flags = split_flags(tokens, 2, {players = true, delay = true})
96	                local tech_name = positional[1]
97	                if not tech_name then
98	                    caller.print("Usage: /mts-debug research <tech> [--players a,b,c] [--delay N]")
99	                    return
100	                end
101	                local players = resolve_players(flags.players, caller)
102	                if not players then return end
103	                local delay = tonumber(flags.delay or "0")
104	                if not delay or delay < 0 then
105	                    caller.print("--delay must be a non-negative integer (ticks)."); return
106	                end
107	
108	                local force_names, seen = {}, {}
109	                for _, p in ipairs(players) do
110	                    local fn = p.force.name
111	                    if not seen[fn] then seen[fn] = true; force_names[#force_names + 1] = fn end
112	                end
113	
114	                local found_on
115	                for _, fn in ipairs(force_names) do
116	                    local f = game.forces[fn]
117	                    if f and f.technologies[tech_name] then found_on = fn; break end
118	                end
119	                if not found_on then
120	                    caller.print("Technology '" .. tech_name
121	                        .. "' not found on any of the target forces.")
122	                    return
123	                end
124	
125	                local id = debug_engine.schedule_research(force_names, tech_name, delay)
126	                local plan = {}

128	                    plan[#plan + 1] = string.format("  +%d ticks: %s", (i - 1) * delay, fn)
129	                end

131	                    "[mts-debug] Scheduled task #%d: research %s on %d force(s):\n%s",
132	                    id, tech_name, #force_names, table.concat(plan, "\n")))
133	                return
134	            end
135

5	-- Admin-only debug task engine. Runs a queue of scheduled one-shot
6	-- actions across future ticks. Powers the /mts-debug console command.
7	--
8	-- Tasks are persisted in storage.debug.tasks and survive save/load.
9	-- Action functions are dispatched by string key (storing function refs
10	-- in storage is forbidden in Factorio).

12	local M = {}
13	
14	local function ensure_storage()
15	    storage.debug = storage.debug or { next_id = 1, tasks = {} }
16	end
17

19	
20	-- ─── Action Implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────
21	-- All actions take an `args` table. Errors are caught and logged so a
22	-- bad task can't break the tick loop.
23	
24	local actions = {}
25	
26	--- Research a technology recursively on a force.
27	--- args = { force = "team-N", tech = "automation" }
28	function actions.research_force(args)
29	    local force = game.forces[args.force]
30	    if not (force and force.valid) then return end
31	    local tech = force.technologies[args.tech]
32	    if not (tech and tech.valid) then return end
33	    tech:research_recursive()
34	end
35	
36	-- ─── Public Scheduling API ────────────────────────────────────────────
37	
38	--- Schedule research_recursive of `tech` on each force in `force_names`,
39	--- spaced `delay_ticks` apart. Returns the task id.
40	function M.schedule_research(force_names, tech, delay_ticks)
41	    ensure_storage()
42	    local base = game.tick + 1
43	    local actions_list = {}
44	    for i, fname in ipairs(force_names) do
45	        actions_list[#actions_list + 1] = {
46	            tick = base + (i - 1) * (delay_ticks or 0),
47	            fn   = "research_force",
48	            args = { force = fname, tech = tech },
49	        }
50	    end
51	    local id = storage.debug.next_id
52	    storage.debug.next_id = id + 1

strings.text: When enabled, new players wait in the Landing Pen before spawning into the game.
When enabled, players in the Landing Pen can request to join an existing team.
When enabled, players can send friend requests. Disabling breaks all existing friendships.
When enabled, all players are notified when someone starts or stops spectating.
When enabled, animated text popups appear on spawn, team join, milestones, and player death.

When enabled, each player sets their own global/team chat mode instead of the whole team switching together. The [GLOBAL]/[TEAM] badge next to each name shows which mode that player is in. Flipping this never exposes a private conversation: switching to individual gives every member their team's current mode, and switching back makes a team team-only if any of its members was.

When enabled, players can import external blueprints via chat strings, the blueprint library, and the import-string button. When disabled, those imports are blocked (in-game blueprint creation -- alt-shift-click, copy-paste of placed entities -- still works either way).
When enabled, a new team's clock does not start until the leader clicks "Start Playing". The team is locked out of all game actions until then, but can browse the map. Designed for speedrun servers.

When enabled, players' colours are automatically kept readable and distinct: dark colours are brightened, brown shades are shifted to a vivid orange, and clashing colours are spread apart -- on join and whenever a player changes colour.

When enabled, admins can give individual teams easier settings via per-team modifiers (e.g. peaceful biters), so team times are no longer comparable and record announcements are tagged. Every modifier change is announced to all players. A team that ever receives a modifier is permanently marked non-competitive; returning to competitive mode requires disbanding all marked teams. input.notes: Zero localisation exists in these 12 files: not one {"key"} LocalisedString; every display string is a plain Lua string, so all statuses are 'hardcoded'. Files with no user-visible strings: scripts/blueprint_lock.lua (permission-group manipulation only; "Default" is an engine group identifier), scripts/buddy_store.lua (storage/frame management; frame names are identifiers), scripts/commands.lua (pure facade). Structural points for the localisation plan: (1) Message pipeline helpers live in scripts/helpers.lua (outside this scan) and appear everywhere: helpers.broadcast (server-wide print of a prebuilt string), helpers.colored_name (wraps a name in [color=] rich text), helpers.item_rich_name ([item=] tags), helpers.team_tag / team_tag_with_leader (team labels embedded mid-sentence). Because sentences are assembled around these helper outputs with .., nearly every dynamic message carries concat + rich-text + server-side-string hazards; converting to LocalisedStrings means these helpers must return fragments usable as __1__-style parameters. (2) chunk_trim.notify(caller_idx, msg) delivers to the caller OR broadcasts via game.print if the caller disconnected — trim results are marked visibility 'player' for that reason; chunk_trim.start also returns English error strings as return values (string|nil contract) that commands/admin.lua prints, so localising changes that API contract. (3) The confirm-dialog pipeline (gui/confirm.lua, outside scan) receives title/message/confirm_text/cancel_text as plain strings from both commands/admin.lua and commands/team.lua; it must accept LocalisedString for any of those to localise. Bullet-list confirm messages hardcode \n layout, manual line-wrapping, and one Lua plural pick (count == 1 and "" or "s"). (4) The guard string "This command can only be used by a player." repeats verbatim 10 times across admin.lua/debug_cmd.lua/team.lua (all via game.print, i.e. broadcast when run from server console/RCON); "Team '<x>' does not exist." repeats 4 times; "Usage: ..." lines repeat per command — obvious shared-locale-key candidates. (5) Cross-file consistency constraints: chat_channel.lua announce words TEAM-ONLY/GLOBAL, chat_tag.lua badge words TEAM/GLOBAL (sharing chat_channel's color constants), and the admin-flag tooltip at admin_flags.lua:53 which references "[GLOBAL]/[TEAM]" must all be translated in sync; the staged-start tooltip (admin_flags.lua:63) quotes the "Start Playing" button caption defined elsewhere. (6) player.tag (chat_tag.lua) is a plain string field — it can NEVER carry a LocalisedString, so the badge words will remain one server-chosen language; same for anything routed through helpers.broadcast as prebuilt strings unless converted. (7) The debug task label (debug.lua:55) and detail are English strings persisted in storage at schedule time and replayed later by /mts-debug list — persisted display strings won't retranslate. (8) commands.add_command name and help both accept LocalisedString in Factorio 2.0, so the 13 help texts are directly localisable; the command NAMES themselves (mts-disband, t, etc.) are also the literal tokens players type and are conventionally left untranslated. (9) Plural handling is ad hoc throughout: "(s)" suffixes (surface(s), task(s), player(s), action(s), force(s)), Lua ternary plural picks (admin.lua:140, team.lua:165-167), and an always-plural "item types" in a log line — these need {"...", n} plural-aware locale keys. (10) Fragments built in files outside this scan surface here: teams_data.activity_info().ago_text (admin.lua:132), team_modifiers.describe/marked_badge (team.lua:201-205), team_rename.attempt error strings (team.lua:141), surface_info.gps/location (team.lua:97-98) — the inventory of those source files must cover them.
